problem:
If the expression ${x}^{2}-10x$ is written as $(x-p{)}^{2}+q$, then what are the values of $p$ and $q?$

$p=$
{{field-1}},
$\,q=$
{{field-2}}

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8x+16 & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 4x+{4}^{2} & = \\ (x-4{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-8x+16)+5 & = \\ (x-4{)}^{2}+5 & .\end{aligned}
$$
